# Client-local selection for a ranking endpoint

The previous shadow-validation gate minimized binary log loss while evaluation gave equal weight to each module's AUC. On the archived seven-client all-MLP roster, ask whether selection on local pair ordering can improve later module-level discrimination. All upstream networks were fitted on the remote GPU. Use their frozen calibration predictions on earlier learners and the original two fitted calibration offsets for each module. Compare mixtures with transfer weights 0, .25, .5, .75 and 1. A client selects the highest calibration-AUC weight, favoring closeness to .5 then smaller weights on ties. Adopt the selected weight only if its paired two-sided Bonferroni 95% lower bound for improvement over .5 exceeds zero across the four alternatives within that client. Otherwise retain .5. Compute tie-adjusted positive and negative placements and paired DeLong variance. An ungated calibration-AUC maximizer isolates the effect of this guard. No development outcome enters selection. Keep the original all-MLP fixed mixture and all 31 published prediction columns as controls, including the log-loss-selected blends. No new model fit or client messages are required.

Primary development contrast is equal-module mean AUC on the 8,815 later eligible registrations. Use the parent paired learner-cluster influence calculation with Bonferroni correction across all controls and the archived .02 practical margin plus positive simultaneous lower bound. Report all weights, calibration sizes, decisions and controls. Equal predictions on this cohort are an observed tie. This is a new decision rule on previously examined OULAD 2014J outcomes. It is not a new temporal confirmation or evidence about additional institutions.
